tool.name: VerticalIntegration
tool.summary: Vertical integration: converts magnetic anomalies into gravity-like (pseudo-gravity) anomalies with the same decay with distance from the source, for comparison or joint interpretation with gravity. Best applied to a magnetic grid that has been reduced to the pole (RTP) or the equator (RTE).
tool.usage:
Also useful for stitched grids with very different line spacing.

Requires a projected (metre-based) coordinate system.

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: out_raster
param.dialogReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.
param.pythonReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.

param.name: max_wn
param.dialogReference: Highest wavenumber kept (radians per map unit); higher wavenumbers are clipped to it to limit noise. 0 = no limit.
param.pythonReference: Highest wavenumber kept (radians per map unit); higher wavenumbers are clipped to it to limit noise. 0 = no limit.

param.name: min_wn
param.dialogReference: Lowest wavenumber used (radians per map unit), so the integration filter (1/k) does not blow up at the longest wavelengths. 0.0001 matches the QGIS plugin.
param.pythonReference: Lowest wavenumber used (radians per map unit), so the integration filter (1/k) does not blow up at the longest wavelengths. 0.0001 matches the QGIS plugin.

param.name: buffer_size
param.dialogReference: FFT buffer in pixels added around the grid before the Fourier transform, to reduce edge effects. 0 (the default) chooses it as in QGIS: the shorter side of the grid, up to 5000. A value greater than 0 is used as that upper limit instead.
param.pythonReference: FFT buffer in pixels added around the grid before the Fourier transform, to reduce edge effects. 0 (the default) chooses it as in QGIS: the shorter side of the grid, up to 5000. A value greater than 0 is used as that upper limit instead.
